text:
sam: quick report — hitting a weird async/init bug with the Python SDK in our FastAPI app. tokens are bleeding between requests and tests show "Unclosed AsyncClient" warnings. stack traces mention event loop mismatch.

lee: can you paste a tiny repro? is the client created at import time?

sam: yep, minimal repro below — app creates a global client during module import and reuses it in handlers. sometimes the Authorization header is from previous request. also get RuntimeError: Cannot run the event loop while another loop is running in some test runs.

sam: ```python
# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from redwood import AsyncRedwoodClient

client = AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key=...)  # created at import time
app = FastAPI()

@app.post('/do')
async def do_stuff(req: Request):
    token = req.headers.get('authorization')
    # SDK uses contextvar for auth inside client, but when client was init'd in sync context it attached background tasks
    resp = await client.generate(..., headers={ 'authorization': token })
    return resp.json()
```

mia: two thoughts: 1) creating an AsyncClient at import time can bind background tasks/transport to the loop active during import. ASGI servers (uvicorn) create their own loop per worker. 2) if the SDK stores auth on the client instance instead of per-request, you'll see header leakage.

cheng: agree. httpx AsyncClient shouldn't be created on import in code that will run under a different event loop. Typical fixes: lazy-init client on first await, or create at startup (lifespan) and close on shutdown. Also don't stash per-request tokens on the client object — read from a contextvar or pass per-call.

lee: are we seeing this in CI or only locally?

sam: both. CI runs pytest with asyncio plugin and we see "RuntimeError: Task attached to a different loop" and unclosed-client warnings. Tests that run sequentially sometimes share headers.

mia: for immediate mitigation: 1) in app startup handler create AsyncClient and store on app.state, 2) ensure shutdown closes client with await client.aclose(). For tests, use httpx.AsyncClient as a context manager or explicitly call aclose in fixture finalizer.

cheng: longer-term SDK fix suggestions: 
- Make AsyncRedwoodClient lazy: don't instantiate httpx.AsyncClient until first async call.
- Provide an async context manager API so users can do `async with AsyncRedwoodClient(...) as client:` and guarantee proper lifecycle.
- Remove any global mutable auth on the client; accept per-call headers or an auth hook that reads a contextvar.
- Add clear docs/examples showing correct startup/shutdown patterns for FastAPI/Starlette.

sam: +1. I'll open a PR with lazy-init + context manager. also going to add a test that simulates two concurrent requests with different tokens to catch regressions.

lee: ping me on the PR for review. also consider adding a runtime check that raises a helpful error if client is created in a different loop than it's used in (detect via asyncio.get_running_loop()).

build-bot: CI failed on branch sam/async-client-lazy-init — failing test: tests/test_async_client.py::test_token_isolated (timeout)

sam: noted, I'll debug the failing test; may be a race in our fixture. will push a fix soon. :bug: :eyes:

mia: thanks for flagging this. small follow-ups: update migration note in changelog and add a short example for FastAPI startup/shutdown.

cheng: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py-sdk/issues/621 to track design and follow-ups (lazy init, ctxvar auth, docs).

sam: thanks — I'll link the PR to #621 and leave notes about the failing CI test.

lee: sounds good. keep it small and test-covered and we'll ship a patch. :shipit:
